dialogue_cloze.speaker: Mom:
dialogue_cloze.sentence: I brought you a surprise! Open the box, it's a special _____ for you.
dialogue_cloze.hint: Something given with love to celebrate or encourage someone.
dialogue_cloze.translation_es: ¡Te traje una sorpresa! Abre la caja, es un regalo especial para ti.

dialogue_cloze.speaker: Boy:
dialogue_cloze.sentence: Fresh cold lemonade! Only five cents per glass to fund my _____ flight!
dialogue_cloze.hint: A vehicle used to travel past Earth's atmosphere into space.
dialogue_cloze.translation_es: ¡Limonada fresca! ¡Solo cinco centavos por vaso para financiar mi vuelo en cohete!

dialogue_cloze.speaker: Elderly Lady:
dialogue_cloze.sentence: Excuse me young man, those are _____ my cookies you are eating!
dialogue_cloze.hint: Used to emphasize the truth or contrast with a misconception.
dialogue_cloze.translation_es: ¡Disculpe joven, esas son en realidad mis galletas las que se está comiendo!

dialogue_cloze.speaker: Bluey:
dialogue_cloze.sentence: Even if we don't speak the same words, we can still be best _____ !
dialogue_cloze.hint: People who share affection, trust, and companionship.
dialogue_cloze.translation_es: ¡Incluso si no hablamos las mismas palabras, aún podemos ser los mejores amigos!

dialogue_cloze.speaker: Barista:
dialogue_cloze.sentence: Here is your triple espresso. Don't worry about the tip, this one is on the _____ !
dialogue_cloze.hint: Famous idiom meaning the establishment is paying for it.
dialogue_cloze.translation_es: Aquí tiene su espresso triple. No se preocupe por la propina, ¡esta cortesía va por la casa!

dialogue_cloze.speaker: Rescuer:
dialogue_cloze.sentence: Come here little buddy, you are completely _____ now in our warm home.
dialogue_cloze.hint: Protected from or not exposed to danger or harm.
dialogue_cloze.translation_es: Ven aquí pequeño amiguito, estás completamente a salvo ahora en nuestro cálido hogar.

sentence_scramble.solution: We acquire language when we understand messages
sentence_scramble.translation_es: Adquirimos el lenguaje cuando comprendemos los mensajes (Principio de Stephen Krashen).

sentence_scramble.solution: What on earth are you doing here
sentence_scramble.translation_es: ¿Qué demonios estás haciendo aquí? (Expresión coloquial común en animaciones).

sentence_scramble.solution: I have been looking for you all morning
sentence_scramble.translation_es: Te he estado buscando toda la mañana.

sentence_scramble.solution: Don't worry everything is going to be fine
sentence_scramble.translation_es: No te preocupes, todo va a salir bien.

sentence_scramble.solution: The more you listen the easier it gets
sentence_scramble.translation_es: Cuanto más escuchas, más fácil se vuelve (Input Comprensible).

idiom_detective.meaning: Something that is very easy and simple to do.
idiom_detective.cartoon_example: Don't stress about the pilot test; for Pip, it will be a piece of cake!

idiom_detective.meaning: Good luck! (Used traditionally in theater and stage performances).
idiom_detective.cartoon_example: Before the magician stepped on stage in Presto, his assistant whispered: 'Break a leg!'

idiom_detective.meaning: To disclose a secret prematurely or by accident.
idiom_detective.cartoon_example: We planned a surprise birthday party for Grizz, but Panda spilled the beans!
options: Make a mess in the kitchen

idiom_detective.meaning: Feeling slightly ill, tired, or unwell.
idiom_detective.cartoon_example: Gus the little raincloud felt under the weather when his stork partner went away.

idiom_detective.meaning: Happening very rarely or almost never.
idiom_detective.cartoon_example: A short animated film wins an Oscar only once in a blue moon.

idiom_detective.idiom: Hit the nail on the head
idiom_detective.meaning: To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.
idiom_detective.cartoon_example: Stephen Krashen hit the nail on the head when he said language is acquired, not drilled.

audio_listening.sentence: The large ship sailed across the ocean.
audio_listening.hint: Listen carefully to the vowel length: is it a short crisp sound or an elongated sound?

audio_listening.vowel_sound: Voiceless dental fricative /θ/ vs Alveolar plosive /t/
audio_listening.sentence: He counted one, two, and three.
audio_listening.hint: Listen for the tongue-between-teeth soft 'th' sound.

audio_listening.sentence: She thought about her childhood dream.
audio_listening.hint: Listen for the crisp final 't' consonant.

audio_listening.sentence: I can't believe what happened today.
audio_listening.hint: Negatives in English are spoken with heavier stress and pitch drop.
